text: A library stores books and makes them available for readers to borrow. The catalog helps visitors find a title or an author.
A computer program consists of instructions that manipulate data. Variables hold values, while functions organize reusable operations.
During a rainstorm, water falls onto roofs, streets, fields, and trees. Some water flows into streams and some enters the soil.
A good explanation starts with the main idea, defines unfamiliar terms, and works through a concrete example.
To bake a loaf of bread, combine flour, water, yeast, and salt. Allow the dough to rise before placing it in the oven.
An orchestra includes groups of string, woodwind, brass, and percussion instruments. The conductor coordinates their timing.
Scientists make observations, develop hypotheses, and test predictions against measurements. Unexpected results can lead to better explanations.
A train station provides platforms where passengers board and leave trains. Timetables list destinations and departure times.
A balanced paragraph connects each sentence to the previous one. The opening sentence introduces the subject and later sentences develop it.
In a garden, roots absorb water and leaves capture sunlight. Plants also need appropriate temperatures and nutrients.
A map represents selected features of a place using symbols and a scale. A legend explains the meaning of those symbols.
The function takes a list of numbers, adds the entries together, and returns their average. An empty list needs a separate rule.
A bicycle moves when the rider turns the pedals. The chain transfers motion to the rear wheel, and the brakes slow the wheels.
A musical rhythm repeats a pattern of beats. Musicians can vary its speed and emphasis while preserving the underlying pattern.
At the market, people compare products, prices, and quantities. A receipt records the items purchased and the total amount paid.
A telescope collects light from distant objects. Larger lenses or mirrors can gather more light and reveal fainter details.
To compare two measurements fairly, use the same units and describe the conditions under which each measurement was obtained.
A conversation gives each participant a chance to ask questions and respond. Clear replies address what the other person actually said.
A forest contains many interacting organisms. Fallen leaves decompose and return nutrients to the soil.
When writing software, test a small example first. Then check boundary conditions and inputs that should produce an error.
A camera forms an image by collecting light through a lens. Exposure controls affect how bright the recorded image appears.
A bridge carries a road or walkway over an obstacle. Its design depends on the distance, expected load, and surrounding conditions.
A recipe gives a list of ingredients and a sequence of steps. Measuring consistently makes the result easier to reproduce.
The city council discussed a proposed park at the meeting. Residents offered suggestions about paths, shade, and places to sit.
A spreadsheet arranges values in rows and columns. Formulas can calculate totals, differences, and averages from those values.
A story usually introduces a setting and characters before presenting a problem. The ending shows how the situation has changed.
In a laboratory notebook, record the date, procedure, observations, and conclusions. Keep direct measurements separate from interpretations.
A network carries information between connected devices. Protocols specify how messages are structured and exchanged.
The classroom activity asked students to sort objects by shape, then explain the rule they had used.
A hiker packed water, food, a map, and a jacket before setting out. The weather forecast suggested cooler conditions near the summit.
An experiment should state which variable changes, which outcome is measured, and which conditions are held constant.
To revise a draft, check whether the main point is clear. Remove unnecessary repetition and replace vague descriptions with concrete details.
